text:
maria: Hey team, customer can't access the Console (no SSO), wants us to triage a 500 + latency spike. They can share screenshots only. What's the minimal reqid/trace info we can ask for from non-technical users?

sam: Ask for the small red error banner screenshot + the response headers visible in the app/network tab if they can. If not, ask for the exact time (UTC) and route they hit.

maria: They can't get developer tools. It's an Android webview within their mobile app. Any quick non-dev steps?

jordan: For webview: ask them to long-press the request in the app's error screen (if present) and copy "Request ID" or "Trace" text. Many apps surface it. If not, ask them to take a screenshot of the network error UI and the approximate timestamp.

lee-bot: tip: header keys we look for -> x-rw-req, x-request-id, x-rw-reqref, request-id.

maria: Ok sending to customer: "Can you please: (1) take a screenshot of the error screen INCLUDING any small footer text, (2) open Settings > App info > Storage and note last crash time, (3) if possible send the exact wall-clock time (UTC) when you tried the request?" Is that enough?

sam: Good start. Also ask them to capture a HAR or proxy dump if they can — but offer a simpler fallback: ask them to reproduce the error and then send one of the following strings copied from the UI: "request id: <alphanumeric>" OR "trace: <hex>". We can correlate from time+route without headers sometimes.

jordan: If they can run a simple curl (non-devs might hand it to an IT person), provide a safe redacted example they can run:

```bash
curl -i 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"input":"test"}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

Ask them to paste the full response headers (NOT the Authorization value). They should redact tokens first.

maria: Also want to request a debug token / snapshot if available — how to guide them?

jordan: For customers without console access we can create a short-lived debug token for them. Steps to request from customer: tell them to reproduce, then reply with the exact UTC time + route + any request id string they saw. We create the debug token and tell them to hit a specific test endpoint that will echo a debug token in the response header. 

sam: If the customer can install a tiny proxy (Charles/Fiddler) that's ideal. But for quick triage: 1) give us timestamp (UTC) 2) route/path 3) any small alphanumeric label in screenshot. We will search our logs with time +/- 2 minutes and route.

maria: I'll send a single copy-paste to the customer. Draft message: "Hi — sorry about the trouble. To help us find your request please: 1) Reproduce the error and take a screenshot of the error screen (include any small footer text). 2) Copy any small string you see that looks like an ID (e.g., a short hex or alpha-numeric). 3) Tell us the exact time in UTC when this happened and which button/flow you used. If you have an IT contact, you can run this redacted curl and share the response headers (please redact Authorization): [paste example]." Any edits?

jordan: Add "If you see a header labelled x-request-id or x-rw-reqref please paste it exactly". Also add a one-line how-to for iOS sysdiagnose: Settings > Privacy > Analytics & Improvements > Share iOS Analytics (but only if they are comfortable).

sam: final note: remind them not to share API keys. Also say we can create a debug token on our side if they prefer — include expected turnaround (usually same-day).

maria: Thanks — sending now. I'll include a tiny checklist and the curl snippet. Will create a debug token offer if they can't get headers. :thumbsup:
